posts.title: Why I wrote 'Production Is Cheap. Trust Is Scarce.'
posts.metaTitle: Why I wrote 'Production Is Cheap. Trust Is Scarce.' | SolCrys Founder Note
posts.description: A short note from SolCrys Cofounder & CPO Eason Wang on the field essay he just published on brand survival in AI-first discovery — what prompted it, and the one shift in CMO thinking it's trying to force.
posts.dek: A note from our CPO on the field essay we just published, and the one shift in CMO thinking it's trying to force.

heroImage.name: Eason Wang
heroImage.alt: Eason Wang, Co-Founder & CPO at SolCrys

posts.leadParagraph: Over the last several quarters, almost every marketing leader we talk to has asked some version of the same question: 'AI is making content cheap — should we be producing more, or differently?' My honest answer keeps surprising people. So I wrote it down.

body.text: The new piece is called 'Production Is Cheap. Trust Is Scarce.' It is a field note on what changes when AI collapses the cost of producing brand content, and why the brands winning in AI-first discovery are not the ones producing more.

The core argument in one sentence: AI made content cheap. It also made trust — the scarce resource that decides who gets cited, recommended, and bought — radically more concentrated and harder to earn.
Why this argument, and why now
Three things converged that pushed me to write this.

First, the numbers got hard to ignore. ChatGPT crossed 900 million weekly active users in February 2026 — more than doubling in twelve months. Lovable hit $400M ARR in the same month with 146 employees. The audience reading AI-generated answers and the cost of producing the content that feeds them have both moved by an order of magnitude in a year. Marketing budgets haven't.

Second, the citation distribution is doing the work of a thesis. The most recent independent analysis we trust — 5W Public Relations' Q1 2026 audit of roughly 600,000 ChatGPT citations — shows Wikipedia and Reddit accounting for more than 25% of all ChatGPT citations in the U.S. The Wall Street Journal, The New York Times, Bloomberg, and the Financial Times do not appear in the top 20. The entire major-publisher class — outlets that have spent a century building the institutional version of trust — has been locked out. That is not a slogan. That is the data.

Third, the conversations on the customer side keep repeating. The most-asked question we get from prospects is 'how much more content should we produce?' In almost every case, the honest answer is less, but governed. The brands gaining citation share fastest in our customer base have cut their content output and re-routed the freed-up budget into a different layer entirely — corporate context, governed prompts, multi-engine measurement, closed-loop execution, and claim governance. That is the new substrate. Production is no longer the bottleneck.
The one shift the essay tries to force

If you read the full piece and only take one thing from it, I would want it to be this: every brand asset you publish in 2026 now has three audiences — the reader, the AI engine, and the brand-governance function. Assets that only serve the first one are legacy assets. Most brand content today is legacy content.

The next 24 months of brand work, in our view, is mostly the transition from the second to the first. We are building SolCrys to make that transition operational — for brands and for the agencies and platform teams that serve them.
Read the full field note

The longform essay walks through what has already happened versus what hasn't, why the citation distribution proves trust is scarce, the four gaps that decide whether AI engines adopt brand content, a 180-day playbook for CMOs starting from zero, and seven questions to ask of any marketing tool you evaluate this year. You can read it on the SolCrys resources site under Strategy & Positioning: Production Is Cheap. Trust Is Scarce.
If you disagree with any of it, I'd rather hear that than agreement. The category is moving fast. Some of what we wrote will be wrong inside a year. The shape of the migration won't be.

posts.title: SolCrys Names Raejeanne Skillern, Former AWS CMO and Intel Leader, as Strategic Advisor
posts.metaTitle: SolCrys Names Raejeanne Skillern as Strategic Advisor | SolCrys News
posts.description: Veteran tech executive Raejeanne Skillern, former AWS CMO and longtime Intel data center leader, joins SolCrys as a strategic advisor as the company builds the AEO operating system for brands in AI search.
posts.dek: Veteran tech executive joins SolCrys to help brands get discovered and recommended in AI search.

heroImage.name: Raejeanne Skillern
heroImage.alt: Portrait of Raejeanne Skillern, Strategic Advisor at SolCrys

posts.leadParagraph: SolCrys, the AEO operating system for brands to win discovery in AI, today announced that Raejeanne Skillern — former Chief Marketing Officer at Amazon Web Services and a longtime hyperscale infrastructure leader — has joined the company as a strategic advisor.

body.text: Skillern brings more than 30 years of leadership across cloud, data center infrastructure, communications, and artificial intelligence. She has led multi-billion-dollar businesses at AWS, Intel, and Flex. Skillern currently serves on the boards of Jabil (NYSE: JBL) and Dycom Industries (NYSE: DY).

Raejeanne brings a rare combination of operating experience, market insight, and board-level perspective at a moment when AI is reshaping how companies build and grow their brands. As organizations across industries adapt to AI-driven discovery and decision-making, her experience scaling global businesses and guiding technology transformation will be invaluable to SolCrys and the customers we serve.

At AWS, Skillern led the global marketing organization, helping to modernize marketing for AI. At Flex, she ran a multi-billion P&L as President of the Communications, Enterprise & Cloud Division, repositioning the business for cloud, optical, and 5G. Over 25 years at Intel, she built the hyperscale data center business alongside the world's leading cloud providers.

AI answer engines are changing how customers discover, evaluate, and choose companies, but most organizations are not yet equipped to manage their presence in this new environment. SolCrys gives companies a clear way to measure how they appear across AI platforms, identify what needs improvement, strengthen their visibility, and track results — while staying true to their brand. SolCrys is building the category-defining platform for how companies manage brand visibility and trust in the AI era.
About SolCrys

SolCrys was founded by a team of AI, data, search, marketing, and growth veterans from Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Alibaba, and Tencent, building the AEO operating system for the next era of brand discovery. The company today serves brands across HPC, AI, consumer goods, retail, and beyond.

posts.title: Welcoming Raejeanne Skillern to SolCrys
posts.metaTitle: Welcoming Raejeanne Skillern to SolCrys | Founder Note
posts.description: A note from SolCrys CEO Gwen Chen on why Raejeanne Skillern — former AWS CMO and longtime Intel hyperscale leader — is joining SolCrys as a strategic advisor, and what it signals about where the company is headed.
posts.dek: A note from our founder on why Raejeanne is joining — and what it signals about where the AEO category, and SolCrys, are headed.

heroImage.name: Raejeanne Skillern
heroImage.alt: Raejeanne Skillern, newly joined SolCrys strategic advisor

posts.leadParagraph: When we started SolCrys, we made a bet that AI answer engines would fundamentally change how customers discover, evaluate, and choose brands — and that most marketing teams weren't equipped for that shift yet.

body.text: Nine months in, that bet is no longer speculative. Buyers are starting product research in ChatGPT instead of Google. Shoppers are getting recommendations from Amazon Rufus and Walmart Sparky before they see a listing. Google AI Mode is changing search from a list of links into AI-generated answers that increasingly shape how customers discover brands. The companies winning are the ones treating AI visibility as something they can measure, diagnose, fix, and prove — not a black box.
That is the operating system we are building at SolCrys. And today, I'm thrilled to share that Raejeanne Skillern is joining us as a strategic advisor.
Why Raejeanne, and why now

Raejeanne spent more than 30 years inside the buildout of modern cloud infrastructure — at Intel, where she built the hyperscale data center business alongside AWS, Azure, and Google; at Flex, where she ran a multi-billion-dollar P&L for cloud, optical, and 5G; and most recently as CMO at AWS, where she led marketing through the early phase of the generative AI shift.

She has seen, more than almost anyone in the industry, how an inflection point in infrastructure rewrites how every category gets sold. That perspective is exactly what we need right now, for three main reasons.
1. She understands what changes when a category moves from search-led to recommendation-led discovery.

The buyer journey for cloud compute did not simply change — the entire vendor evaluation framework changed. The same shift is now happening for consumer brands, B2B software, retail SKUs, and professional services inside the AI answer layer. Most of our customers are still operating with SEO-era playbooks. Raejeanne has lived through this kind of transition before, and she can help us help them.
2. She has scaled marketing organizations that operate as one team alongside product and sales.

Answer Engine Optimization is not just an SEO-team problem. It requires collaboration across SEO, PMM, brand, communications, PR, product, and sales. SolCrys is built to be the connective tissue between these teams, and Raejeanne has built the operating models that make this kind of cross-functional execution work at scale.
3. She brings board-level perspective at exactly the right time for SolCrys.

Raejeanne sits on the boards of Jabil (NYSE: JBL) and Dycom Industries (NYSE: DY). The questions boards are now asking about AI exposure — what is our visibility, where are we losing share, is this measured — are exactly the questions SolCrys is built to answer. Having someone on the team who thinks about technology adoption from both sides of the boardroom table sharpens how we build, what we prioritize, and how we define the category.
What this signals for the brands we serve
If you're a customer, advisor, partner, or prospect reading this: Raejeanne's involvement is a signal of where we're investing. Over the next two quarters we are doubling down on three things.

items: Cross-engine measurement depth — moving beyond mention and citation counting to true Share of Recommendation and answer-accuracy tracking, prompt-by-prompt, across ChatGPT, Gemini, Google AI Overviews / AI Mode, Perplexity, Amazon Rufus, Walmart Sparky, and ChatGPT Shopping.

Corporate Context as the brand operating layer — ensuring every action SolCrys recommends is grounded in your approved stats, claims, and guardrails by default, so your content stays on-brand, accurate, and defensible.

The execution loop — closing the gap between 'we found the gap' and 'we fixed it', with draft briefs to media outlets, analysts and influencers, FAQ updates, and content actions tied to measurable movements in AI answers.

body.text: Closing

I started SolCrys with my co-founders Eason and Jia because we believed brand discovery was about to be rewritten, and the teams building inside that change deserved a real operating system, not another dashboard.
Bringing Raejeanne onto the team will help us better serve our customers as they navigate this next phase of AI discovery.
Welcome, Raejeanne. We're thrilled to have you with us.
